title: Scape
summary: clean but very unoriginal launch video
text:
clean but very unoriginal launch video

- very very clean animations that look like the real product. extremely well done
- 18 months social proof is interesting

but
- takes a long time to get to the killer feature
- uninteresting intro - we all hate email and dont care you hired a team
- we've seen all of this already

ok so these guys launched a product that has been done a million times over with no features that make it stand out

its a situation a lot of other founders may find themselves in

my advice would be twofold
1. build ONE unique killer feature to emphasize. will help your product and help your launch video
2. ensure your script is conscious of what your audience has seen already

if you really need to launch without doing #1, you are going to need to find a way to say "all the other products you tried don't work, but ours does" 

if you don't do any of this, it comes off very tone def and derivative. 

still a very well executed video editing wise. congrats on the launch either way!

title: Death Clock
text:
hilarious and genius launch video

- so funny - burying the body is genius
- founder is great in front of the camera
- great use of AI (eg the horse)
- so much social proof - smart to open with the news stories, the 10k stars, etc
- great pacing
- great 1 liners everywhere "i can tell you the date youre gonna die" "live long enough to see your babies babies have some babies" "know your date... change your fate"
- script is perfect. so many zingers.
- music is funny and apt
- nice and fast
- smart to have the URL in bottom left the whole time
- good editing with logos and text behind him and stop in the beginning
- body bag thing keeps your attention the whole time - you want to see what he does with it

but
- might have emphasized the free blood test. that sounds killer and is quickly passed over.
- might have shown the app, but honestly not necessary.

this is our era's Dollar Shave Club launch video. 

people have tried to emulate the vibe of that video forever and this is the first that did it (and exceeded).

being funny is very very hard to pull off. but having a fun brand and product like Death Clock makes it 100x easier. in cases like these, the script writes itself. so this video was going to be good by default, but they really took it to the next level.

if you're thinking about doing a funny video, study this one as much as you can.

one thing I'd highlight is how dynamic it is. lots of different scenes and juicy edits and jokes on each to keep them interesting. and the whole video drives towards revealing what he does with the body bag.

probably the best launch video I've seen all year and since I started reviewing launch videos.

amazing work

- visual embellishment - could have done something like transitioned the scene to have the character on a pedestal with light shining down on it for 3 seconds before going back to the office scene.

title: PromptQL
summary: big PR screw up launch video
text:
big PR screw up launch video

- script is super optimized
- good social proof
- lotta ADHD food

but
- narration is too fast and under their breath
- comes off as really fake - animations instead of UI, massive raise, meme accounts driving engagement, etc
- I'm veryyyy tired of this format

good example of a launch video that can backfire. 

some folks dug up the fact that this company appears to be a pivot from a Series C company. pivots are fine, but stretching the truth around it is not.

if you have something as big as a $136M round to announce, you better be prepared for people to ask how and why... especially if your product is unknown and generic and you don't share the investors' names....

as @lulumeservey says, you get cancelled when people feel like you're overrated - your hype/funding exceeds how good you/your product is. and this team walked right into this.

they could have had an even more viral video just telling the truth: "we shut down our $800M company to go all in on this idea" is way better.

I feel bad for these founders though. 

judging by the clickbaity script, overdone animations, and heavy use of meme accounts, its possible that the agency they worked with pressured them into using the $136M number.

as a founder you have to remember, agencies incentives aren't always aligned to yours. many focus on numbers, not outcomes or qualitative impact.

so in summary, dont do this. please tell the truth.

josh / browser co is the king of video. hands down the best of the best. if you want to create great videos just study them and hire whoever they worked with.

too much to comment on what is great about this, but the big thing they do really well is energy management.

just like an amazing DJ uses slower/faster happier/more sad music to bring their audience on a journey, josh and co do that here very well.

starts calm, then gets chaotic (VERY chaotic), then the music stops and you enter the calm. you associate their brand with calm because it is the resolution to the chaos.

increasing volume + more distinct sounds + rising pitches + faster clips + minor or discordant music = chaos

minimalism across the board and major / soft music = release

use this!

amazing work as always josh/team.

text:

- lighting is really nice

but

every startup is doing video now. all of them.

it is anti-sprezzatura - communicates "we only care about making this go viral," which hurts for intelligent / brand sensitive audiences like investors and founders.

basically, excellent execution but lets try something different?

the best launch videos are ones that reflect the personality and vision of the founder so much that it would be impossible for anyone else to copy.

this video is very much me: happy, sunny, chaotic, ADHD, funny, weird, approachable, musical, imperfect.

best advice for myself going forward to to keep being me but balance it more with what viewers and customers need to feel what I feel about our product.
